scope: READ-ONLY follow-up diagnosis (Creator option E). No worldgen, engine, map, law or shipped-data change; no option chosen; no fix implemented.
notes: Windows are entered through a QA inspection landing (qaUsed=true) purely so a real RunState and therefore the real blockGrid/source layer exist. QA landings are never playable evidence.

E1 reconstructs only the two inputs of the compile eligibility flood (padded walkable, padded anchors) and never re-runs source drawing, because the draw is global-keyed and therefore cannot differ per window. The reconstruction is validated before it is believed.
E2 reads every authored POI in the frame, so its blast-radius counts are complete for authored compounds and make no claim about procedural (non-authored) POIs beyond what it measures.

compileReachedIsUnionOfAnchorFloods.text: const reached=new Uint8Array(n); for(const s of m.starts){const d=reachable(m,s.x,s.y);if(d[s.y*m.width+s.x]<0) errors.push(`start ${s.id} is not walkable`);for(let i=0;i<n;i++)if(d[i]>=0)reached[i]=1;}

compileDrawHashUsesGlobal.text: for(const [key,p] of Object.entries(rates)){ const u=Math.max(hash2(gx,gy,salt ^ stableHash(key)),1e-9);const score=-Math.log(u)/p;if(score<best){best=score;choice=key;} }

compileBlockerCompetitionIsExtentBound.text: const accepted=new Uint8Array(n);for(const i of blockers){const x=i%m.width,y=Math.floor(i/m.width);if(OFFSETS.some(([dx,dy])=>accepted[(y+dy)*m.width+x+dx]))out[i]=null;else accepted[i]=1;}

compileIsolationCleanupFloodsFromStarts.text: const accessible = new Uint8Array(n); for (const start of m.starts) { const d=reachable({...m,walkable:pass},start.x,start.y); for(let i=0;i<n;i++) if(d[i]>=0) accessible[i]=1; }

padConstant.text: const PAD = 8, PW = WW + PAD * 2, PH = WH + PAD * 2, PN = PW * PH;

pAnchorRequiresWalkable.text: if (pWalk[py * PW + px]) pAnchors.push({ id: `g_${gx}_${gy}`, x: px, y: py });

paddedPoiTileClip.text: if (px >= 0 && py >= 0 && px < PW && py < PH) paddedPoiTiles.set(py * PW + px, t);

paddedOrigin.text: const paddedWin: WindowSpec = { originTx: win.originTx - PAD, originTy: win.originTy - PAD, w: PW, h: PH };

interiorLocalKey.text: const KEY = (x: number, y: number) => y * WW + x;

landmarkRejectedNearBorder.text: if (cx <= 1 || cy <= 1 || cx >= WW - 2 || cy >= WH - 2) return false;

counterfactual.scoredOn: every sampled non-salvage source disagreement cell, as a 2x2 against the shipped policy
counterfactual.reading: This scores only the COMPILE-SIDE flood, which the ladder below shows is the smaller part of the problem. A policy that removes a compile-side flood difference does not by itself guarantee identical output: the per-cell draw is global-keyed, but the blocker competition and the isolation cleanup inside compileEconomy remain extent-bound.
